scenes.heading: Client Libraries — Advanced Features (Part 1 of 2)
scenes.narration: Templates. Client Libraries — Advanced Features (Part 1 of 2). In this video we review 6 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: How are client libraries loaded in AEM as a Cloud Service?
scenes.heading: HTL, via the helper template at libs/granite/sightly/templates/clientlib.html — the only method current AEMaaCS docs describe
scenes.body: In AEM as a Cloud Service, client libraries are loaded through HTL, using the helper template at libs/granite/sightly/templates/clientlib.html, accessed via data-sly-use and invoked with data-sly-call, passing the desired categories. Current Cloud Service documentation only covers this approach.

scenes.question: What is the HTL syntax pattern for loading a client library by category?
scenes.heading: data-sly-use.clientlib="libs/granite/sightly/templates/clientlib.html", then data-sly-call passing categories
scenes.body: The pattern is: use data-sly-use to instantiate the clientlib helper template, then data-sly-call to invoke it (e.g. clientlib.css or clientlib.all), passing the desired categories as an array or comma-separated string.

scenes.question: Is the older JSP taglib approach (ui:includeClientLib) still a current, valid way to load clientlibs in AEMaaCS?
scenes.heading: It's a legacy, on-premise-era pattern — current AEMaaCS Cloud Service documentation doesn't reference it, and cloud component scripting is HTL-only
scenes.body: The JSP taglib pattern using ui:includeClientLib is legacy, historical context from on-premise AEM. AEM as a Cloud Service component development is HTL-only, and the current Cloud Service documentation for client libraries doesn't reference the JSP approach at all.

scenes.question: What does the dependencies property on a cq:ClientLibraryFolder node do?
scenes.heading: A String[] property listing the categories of other client library folders that the current one depends on
scenes.body: The dependencies property is a String[] listing other client library categories that the current library folder depends on — useful when code in one folder requires a file in another to function properly.

scenes.question: What effect does the dependencies property have on the HTML generated by ui:includeClientLib (or its HTL equivalent)?
scenes.heading: It generates HTML that includes a link to your library file as well as links to its declared dependencies
scenes.body: When you link a client library folder that declares dependencies, the generated HTML includes a link to your generated library file as well as links to its dependencies, ensuring all required resources load together.

scenes.question: What does the embed property on a client library folder do?
scenes.heading: The embedding library's generated JS/CSS files include the code from the embedded library at runtime
scenes.body: The embed property lets you embed code from one client library into another — at runtime, the generated JS and CSS files of the embedding library will include the code from the embedded library.
